Tomorrow's lowest net load block runs six hours or longer.

📉 Once wind and solar are taken out of the load plan for 20 November 2026, net load bottoms out twice, at 21,740 MWh at 04:00 and 21,778 MWh at 12:00, and is highest from 17:00 to 20:59, where it holds between 36,512 and 38,448 MWh. ⚙️ LOWEST NET LOAD. 01:00 to 07:59, seven unbroken hours in the very low band, with the wind forecast holding between 10,305 and 10,519 MWh through them. Across the comparison days, the lower of the two prices, Market Clearing Price (MCP) and System Marginal Price (SMP), was at or under 150 TL/MWh in 18 of the 210 block hours, spread over 5 separate days.

⚙️ HIGHEST NET LOAD. 17:00 to 20:59, the block that carries the day's heaviest net load, with the load plan at 46,134 MWh at 17:00. Across the comparison days, the higher of MCP and SMP reached the 4,500 TL/MWh cap in 43 of the 120 block hours, spread over 16 separate days.

🔎 WHAT STANDS OUT
All four evening hours from 17:00 to 20:59 sit in the very high band, and across them the wind forecast falls from 7,451 MWh at 17:00 to 6,590 MWh at 20:00.

💡 What it means: the plants that fill in after wind and solar sit at a low level for a long stretch of the day.

METHOD
📐 Net load = load plan − wind forecast − solar

📊 Bands: net load quintiles of the comparison days, not of the target day; block statistics use the block hours on each comparison day

⚡ Balancing cost 15,706,556 TL, measured as value against the day-ahead price. Constraint-coded instructions were 73.6 MWh of 18,930 MWh instructed in total. The largest positive hourly cost came at 09:00, an up-regulation hour: on the published supply curve, buying that volume in the day-ahead market would have lifted the clearing price to the price cap, above the 4,487 TL/MWh system marginal price (SMP), so day-ahead would have cost more.

📆 Versus 4 November 2026, the same weekday one week earlier: the daily average price was 6.7% lower and wind generation 14.4% higher.

In Türkiye, how low the day-ahead price falls at midday follows what fossil plants have left to cover, not demand. Demand at 12:00 does not line up: 4 November had the least of the three and still cleared above 11 November. The residual already nets out solar and the other renewables; solar alone, and hydro, wind and other renewables alone, rank the three days in the same order, an equal fit.
